siteRecommendations: Every illustration in this pass is owner-supplied, photorealistic and depicts the subject of its record. Each carries a caption that states what it is not, because a realistic illustration on an evidence-first site has to disprove itself in words.

Four live photographs are still only indirectly related to their stories and are queued for replacement by story-specific illustrations: the iQFOiL class photo of another sailor, the 2002 Yanbu astronaut photograph, the April 2025 Rafah archival photograph, and the Beaufort Castle photograph.

Records still without any image after this pass: the H.R. 4795 university-boycott bill, the Iraq helicopter claim, the four daily briefs of September 1 to 8, the shelter-data correction, the Lebanese detainee handover, and the twelve stubs rewritten as pointers.

research.topic: Editorial illustration for records without imagery
research.focus: Eight live records carrying no hero, briefed as concrete scenes rather than abstract metaphors after the first briefs were rejected as unrelated to their stories
research.conclusion: Eight photorealistic illustrations were produced to brief and attached, each depicting the actual subject of its record. Every caption names what the image is not, and every rights block records in-house generation with the file hash.

vetoes.candidate: The first set of illustration briefs, built on abstract metaphors such as glowing nodes, translucent layers and empty pedestals
vetoes.reason: Rejected by the owner as having no connection to the content. An image the desk generates itself has no excuse to be generic, so the briefs were rewritten to describe the real place, object and situation of each story. The abstract cinema illustration produced from the first brief was never attached to a record and has been removed from the delivery branch.
